newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court gives states rights over unemployment benefits.
newsitem.headline: Court gives states rights over unemployment benefits.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday member states may refuse unemployment benefits to European Union citizens if a period of contribution or employment has not been completed in that member state.

Three workers who moved to Spain without jobs sought unemployment benefits. They recieved benefits for six months, and during that time Spain paid contributions on their behalf to the sickness insurance and family benefits schemes.
When the workers applied to receive unemployment allowance for claimants over 52 years of age, they were denied because they had not contributed for the minimum period required under Spanish law.

Spain argued that it cannot be right that any worker reaching the age of 52 who has acquired entitlement to a pension under the legislation of another member state might go to Spain to receive unemployment benefits, without ever contributing to the Spanish social security system.
As to whether the contribution paid by Spain during the receipt of unemployment constitutes a period of insurance under Spanish law, the court said it is for the national court to decide.

"The court has consistently held member states remain competent to define the conditions for granting social security benefits, even if they make them more strict, provided the conditions adopted do not give rise to overt or disguised discrimination between Community workers," the court said.

The court said workers moving throughout the EU cannot rely on Community rules governing retirement pension qualification, under article 48 of the Council of Ministers regulation 1408/71, when seeking unemployment benefits.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Spanish)
"Articles 48 and 51 of the EC Treaty - Articles 4, 48 and 67 of regulation (EEC) No 1408/71 - Unemployment benefit for persons over 52 years of age"
Joined Cases C-88/95, C-102/95 and C-103/95
References from the Juzgado de lo Social de Santiago de Compostela (Spain) for a preliminary ruling between
Bernadina Martinez Losada, Manuel Fernandez Balado and Jose Paredes
and
Instituto Nacional de Empleo (Inem) and
Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS)

on the interpretation of articles 4, 48 and 67 of Council regulation (EEC) No 1408/71 of 14 June 1971 on the application of social security schemes to employed persons, to self-employed persons and to members of their families moving within the Community, as amended and updated by Council regulation (EEC) No 2001/83 of 2 June 1983 (OJ 1983 L 230, p. 6), as amended by Council regulation (EEC) No 1248/92 of 30 April 1992 (OJ 1992 L 136, p. 7), and of articles 48 and 51 of the EC treaty
THE COURT hereby rules

1. An allowance such as that provided for by the Spanish General Law for unemployed persons of more than 52 years of age constitutes an unemployment benefit within the meaning of article 4(1) of Council regulation (EEC) No 1408/71 of 14 June 1971 on the application of social security schemes to employed persons, to self-employed persons and to members of their families moving within the community, as amended and updated by Council regulation (EEC) No 2001/83 of 2 June 1983 , as amended by Council regulation (EEC) No 1248/92 of 30 April 1992, and of articles 48 and 51 of the EC treaty
2. Article 48 of the aforementioned regulation is not applicable to unemployment benefits.

3. It is for the national court to determine whether the condition laid down by article 67(3) of the aforementioned regulation to the effect that a person who has completed periods of insurance in another member state cannot rely on those periods in order to obtain unemployment benefit in the state concerned unless he last completed periods of insurance in accordance with the provision of the legislation of that state, is fulfilled where the person concerned has never been in employment in that state but contributions have been paid on his behalf to the sicknesws insurance and family benefits schemes by the competent unemplyment institution.

4. It is not contrary to articles 48 and 51 of the EC treaty, or to the aforementioned regulation, for national legislation to require the person concerned to have paid contribuiton for a fifteen-year period to a pension scheme in one or more member state in order to qualify for the grant of an unemployment allowance for claimants of over 52 years of age.
